The first step towards

Devices vision project01
Devices in context
What we build, and why it matters

What we do: the Devices team builds and manages all of Adyen's in-person payment devices, both terminals and mobile (SoftPOS).

Why it matters: in-person payments are €311B, ~23% of Adyen's volume, growing ~35% a year.

The gap: IPP NPS is 57.7 vs 66.2 overall (8.5 points lower) and escalations rose to 3.5%. The experience is the opportunity.

The device lifecycle
  • 01Order & fulfil: order the right hardware, ship, replace and return.
  • 02Onboard & board: bring terminals live and assign them to stores.
  • 03Configure: set payment features, POS limits and branding, via reusable profiles.
  • 04Operate, monitor & update: watch fleet health, fix counter issues, roll out firmware/SDK updates.
  • 05Reassign & retire: move terminals across stores, repair and return.
Dependencies with Channels
  • Devices (backend): runs the terminal and SoftPOS layer; a middleware abstraction layer keeps the fleet vendor-independent.
  • Channels (frontend): owns the unified, device-independent app on top.
  • At runtime: Devices supplies health and diagnostics; Channels renders them on-device as error messages and self-serve actions.
Devices vision project02
Today's scenario
One failed-transaction report, seven surfaces, no answer

Stores call in: "POS transactions failed several times." To find which devices, how often and why, a Lightspeed merchant works through seven separate surfaces in the Customer Area and docs, and still hits a dead end.

Click any step to jump straight to its screenshot in the appendix.

Seven surfaces, one question: why did it fail?
  • 01Stores list. No device view: no way to see which terminals sit under each store.
  • 02Payment list. Hard to consolidate which devices failed, and why: "failed to go online", but is it the network, the device, or the shopper?
  • 03Adyen docs. A code, not a cause; not much explanation.
  • 04Device settings (via a device ID). Wants to see how long it was offline, and whether it is shopper behaviour or a faulty device.
  • 05Terminal timeline. Limited log types, hard to see why it failed, few action points.
  • 06Support ticket. "I give up." The whole investigation is handed to Adyen.
  • 07Export to CSV. Future: to prevent failures and compare other terminals and stores, the only option is Excel, still no insight.
Devices vision project03
The North Star

Today: a dozen CA and back-office pages for the same few actions, fragmented, duplicated and hard to support.

Future: Devices built around jobs, not the tools we've accumulated, with intelligence embedded.

Why we need it: to align on one direction, so each near-term build adds up to a coherent whole.

From today's fragmented journeys to jobs-based surfaces
  • 01Keep my fleet healthy · Fleet health, diagnostics & updates: see the health of every terminal, let store staff fix counter issues before they stop a sale, and roll out firmware/SDK updates safely across the fleet.Fleet health is the first slice we build here.Device intelligence
  • 02Get my devices live · Lifecycle, onboarding & reassignment: order, ship, replace and return terminals (with stock, repairs and warranties), and onboard or reassign them across stores by business need, without part-mapping or assignment errors.Devices & locations
  • 03Adapt devices to my business · Configuration, profiles & engagement: build reusable configuration profiles (Company → Merchant → Store → Device), set payment features and POS limits, brand the terminal screen, and run loyalty, promotions and offers through the device.Device studio (+ intelligence)
AI is the thread across all three surfaces, enabling the entire job to be done, not just showing data.
Ask anything
Query fleet, payments and health in plain language.
Act by prompt
Run fleet actions by describing the outcome.
Next best action
Surfaces what to do next, and why.
Devices vision project04
First building block: Fleet health
Inside Device intelligence, where the pain is sharpest and the data already exists. WIP, 2027.
Why here, and what we're testing
  • Hardware fails at the counter. #1 detractor, ~9,100 tickets.
  • No actionable fleet reporting. Reporting 5.74/7, 2nd-lowest.
  • Troubleshooting is reactive. Most tickets from live-integration merchants.

"Why isn't this terminal working?" · "Which of my stores need attention right now?" · "I can't even see which terminals are locked, or why." Merchant

The design: four building blocks
  • 01Fleet health overview: an at-a-glance view across the fleet.
  • 02What to act on: the device list, down to individual logs.
  • 03Fleet trends: the metrics to improve, over time.
  • 04Stores to watch: which stores need attention, into store status.

Fleet-wide → Store → Single device.

Devices vision project07
Appendix · The scenario
Current pain points

Imagine one of our merchants, a Lightspeed store. Its staff call in: "POS transactions have failed several times." The merchant now has to work out which devices are failing, how often, and why, fast, while shoppers wait to pay. They got no warning in advance, so they have to start looking from scratch.

To answer one question, why did this terminal fail, the merchant hops across seven separate surfaces in the Customer Area and docs, then exports to Excel, and still ends with a support ticket and no root cause. Each surface shows a fragment; none shows the whole picture.

A2
Stores list, but no view of the devices inside
Devices › Stores
You can see the stores, but not which terminals sit inside them, so there is no way to tie the reported failures to a device.
A3
Payment list, but failures won’t consolidate by device
Payments › Payment list
Failures won’t group by device, and “Failed to go online” doesn’t say whether it is network, hardware, or the shopper.
A4
Adyen docs, but not much explanation
Adyen Docs › Raw responses
The docs explain the response code, but not why this terminal failed or what to do next.
A5
Device settings, history but no diagnosis
Devices › Device settings
You can see how long the device was offline, but not enough to tell whether it was the shopper’s behaviour or a fault in the device.
A6
Terminal timeline, limited logs but no cause
Devices › Terminal timeline
Only a few log types are recorded, so the transaction and network failures that would explain “why” never show up, and there is no clear next step.
A7
“I give up” → a ticket, and still no way to get ahead
06Support ticketHand it to Adyen

With no answer from any of the tools, the merchant gives up and opens a support ticket, handing the whole investigation to Adyen. Slow for the merchant, and costly for Support.

07Export to CSVFuture · Payments › Export

Looking ahead, they want to prevent failures and see how other terminals and stores are affected. Today the only option is export to CSV and dig through Excel, which yields little insight.

No alert
No proactive warning before customers feel it
No fleet view
No way to compare across terminals & stores
No trend
No history to spot a pattern building up
